examples: The teacher struggled to control the unruly classroom after the fire alarm went off.
معلم پس از به‌صدا درآمدن هشدار آتش‌نشانی برای کنترل کلاس بی‌نظم و سرکش تلاش زیادی کرد.
Security guards were called in to deal with the unruly crowd outside the stadium.
نگهبانان امنیتی برای مدیریت جمعیت سرکش بیرون از استادیوم فراخوانده شدند.
His unruly hair never stayed in place, no matter how much gel he used.
موهای بی‌نظم او هرچقدر هم ژل می‌زد، هیچ‌وقت سر جای خودش نمی‌ماند.
miniContext: An unruly person, crowd, or object refuses to follow rules or stay under control. Teachers often dread an unruly class full of students who talk over each other and ignore instructions. The word can also describe things that resist order in a more physical sense, such as unruly hair that won't lie flat or an unruly garden overrun with weeds. Whether describing behavior or appearance, unruly always suggests a lack of discipline or order.

examples: The boxer suffered a brutal defeat in the final round of the match.
بوکسور در دور پایانی مسابقه شکستی خشن و بی‌رحمانه متحمل شد.
Critics gave the film a brutal review, calling it the worst movie of the year.
منتقدان نقدی خشن و بی‌رحمانه بر این فیلم نوشتند و آن را بدترین فیلم سال خواندند.
Soldiers described the brutal conditions they faced during the long winter campaign.
سربازان شرایط خشن و سختی را که در طول عملیات طولانی زمستانی تجربه کردند شرح دادند.
miniContext: Something brutal is extremely harsh, cruel, or violent, often causing great pain or suffering. A brutal dictator might rule through fear and violence, while a brutal winter can bring dangerously cold temperatures and relentless storms. People also use the word more loosely to describe anything unpleasantly harsh, such as a brutal work schedule or brutal honesty that hurts to hear. In every case, brutal signals an intensity that goes beyond ordinary difficulty.

examples: A brawl broke out between two rival fans just outside the stadium gates.
یک دعوای فیزیکی بین هواداران دو تیم رقیب درست بیرون از دروازه‌های استادیوم درگرفت.
Police arrived quickly to break up the brawl before anyone got seriously hurt.
پلیس به سرعت رسید تا دعوا را پیش از آنکه کسی به‌طور جدی آسیب ببیند متوقف کند.
The bar owner banned both men after their brawl damaged several tables and chairs.
صاحب بار هر دو مرد را پس از آنکه دعوایشان چند میز و صندلی را خراب کرد، از آمدن منع کرد.
miniContext: A brawl is a rough, disorganized fight, usually involving several people throwing punches rather than a formal match. Brawls often erupt in crowded, emotional settings such as bars, sports events, or political rallies, where tempers run high. Unlike a planned boxing match, a brawl has no rules and can quickly turn chaotic and dangerous. Witnesses to a brawl are often just as shaken as the people involved, since the violence tends to spread unpredictably.

examples: He had to thrust the heavy door open with his shoulder because the lock was stuck.
او مجبور شد با شانه‌اش در سنگین را هل بدهد و باز کند چون قفل آن گیر کرده بود.
The soldier was trained to thrust his bayonet forward in a single swift motion.
سرباز آموزش دیده بود تا سرنیزه‌اش را در یک حرکت سریع به جلو فرو ببرد.
She thrust her hands into her pockets to warm them against the cold wind.
او دستانش را در جیب‌هایش فرو برد تا آن‌ها را در برابر باد سرد گرم کند.
miniContext: To thrust means to push something suddenly and forcefully in a particular direction. A fencer might thrust a sword toward an opponent, while a swimmer could thrust their arms through the water with powerful strokes. The word can also describe someone being unexpectedly placed into a difficult situation, as when a young manager is thrust into a leadership role without warning. Whether physical or figurative, thrust always implies a sudden, forceful movement.

examples: Please duplicate this document and send a copy to each department manager.
لطفاً این سند را کپی کنید و یک نسخه برای هر مدیر بخش ارسال کنید.
The locksmith can duplicate your house key in just a few minutes.
کلیدساز می‌تواند کلید خانه شما را در عرض چند دقیقه کپی کند.
Researchers were unable to duplicate the surprising results of the original experiment.
پژوهشگران نتوانستند نتایج شگفت‌انگیز آزمایش اصلی را دوباره تکرار و کپی کنند.
miniContext: To duplicate something means to make an exact copy of it, whether it's a key, a document, or a set of results. Offices often duplicate important paperwork so that a backup exists in case the original is lost. In science, researchers try to duplicate an experiment's results to confirm that the original findings were accurate and not just a coincidence. When a copy is identical in every detail, people may also call it a duplicate, using the same word as a noun.

examples: She trained harder than ever to beat her biggest rival in the championship race.
او بیش از همیشه تمرین کرد تا بزرگ‌ترین رقیب خود را در مسابقه قهرمانی شکست دهد.
The two companies have been fierce rivals in the smartphone market for a decade.
این دو شرکت برای یک دهه رقیبان سختی در بازار گوشی‌های هوشمند بوده‌اند.
The city's two football clubs have been rivals since they were founded a century ago.
دو تیم فوتبال این شهر از زمان تأسیسشان یک قرن پیش، رقیب یکدیگر بوده‌اند.
miniContext: A rival is a person, team, or company that competes against another for the same goal, prize, or position. Business rivals constantly try to outsell each other, while athletic rivals push each other to train harder and perform better. Sometimes a rivalry grows friendly over time, but other rivals remain bitter competitors for years. Having a strong rival can actually motivate people to improve, since there is always someone to measure themselves against.

examples: The champion studied videos of her next opponent to prepare for the match.
قهرمان ویدیوهای حریف بعدی خود را مطالعه کرد تا برای مسابقه آماده شود.
In the debate, he struggled to respond when his opponent raised an unexpected point.
در مناظره، وقتی حریفش نکته‌ای غیرمنتظره مطرح کرد، او برای پاسخ‌دادن دچار مشکل شد.
The senator's political opponent accused her of breaking several campaign promises.
حریف سیاسی سناتور او را متهم کرد که چند وعده انتخاباتی را زیر پا گذاشته است.
miniContext: An opponent is someone you compete or argue against, whether in a sport, a game, a debate, or an election. A chess player studies an opponent's strategy to predict future moves, while a politician must be ready to counter an opponent's arguments during a public debate. Unlike a rival, who may be a long-term competitor, an opponent can simply be whoever you happen to face in a single match or contest. Respecting your opponent is often considered just as important as trying to win.

examples: The bewildered tourist stared at the map, unable to figure out which street to take.
گردشگر سردرگم به نقشه خیره شده بود و نمی‌توانست بفهمد کدام خیابان را باید برود.
She gave a bewildered look when the teacher asked a question nobody understood.
وقتی معلم سؤالی پرسید که هیچ‌کس آن را نفهمید، او نگاهی سردرگم انداخت.
Completely bewildered by the complicated instructions, he decided to call customer support for help.
او که کاملاً از دستورالعمل‌های پیچیده سردرگم شده بود، تصمیم گرفت برای کمک با پشتیبانی مشتریان تماس بگیرد.
miniContext: Someone who is bewildered feels confused and unable to understand what is happening around them. A bewildered child might freeze in a crowded mall after losing sight of their parents, unsure which way to go. People can also feel bewildered by confusing instructions, strange news, or a sudden change of plans. The feeling of being bewildered usually passes once someone provides a clear explanation or a familiar face appears.

examples: Everyone expected the champions to win easily, but the underdog shocked the crowd with a last-minute goal.
همه انتظار داشتند قهرمانان به‌راحتی ببرند، اما تیم کم‌شانس با گلی در دقایق پایانی تماشاگران را شوکه کرد.
As the underdog in the election, he had far less money for advertising than his opponent.
او به‌عنوان کاندیدای کم‌شانس انتخابات، پول بسیار کمتری برای تبلیغات نسبت به حریفش داشت.
Fans love a good underdog story, where the weaker team overcomes impossible odds to win.
هواداران عاشق داستان‌های تیم کم‌شانسی هستند که با وجود شانس بسیار کم، موفق به بردن می‌شود.
miniContext: An underdog is a person or team that is expected to lose a competition because they seem weaker, less experienced, or less favored than their opponent. Sports fans often cheer loudly for the underdog, hoping to witness a surprising upset over a stronger rival. Movies and novels frequently tell underdog stories because audiences enjoy watching someone overcome the odds against them. Even outside of sports, a small startup company can be called an underdog when it competes against a much larger, established business.

examples: The dog's owner warned visitors that the animal could be vicious if it felt threatened.
صاحب سگ به بازدیدکنندگان هشدار داد که این حیوان اگر احساس تهدید کند می‌تواند خشن و درنده شود.
She became the target of a vicious rumor that spread quickly through the school.
او هدف یک شایعهٔ شرورانه قرار گرفت که به‌سرعت در مدرسه پخش شد.
The boxer landed a vicious uppercut that ended the fight in the third round.
بوکسور یک آپرکات خشن و قدرتمند زد که مبارزه را در دور سوم پایان داد.
miniContext: Something vicious is cruel, aggressive, or intended to cause serious harm, whether physical or emotional. A vicious dog might attack without warning, while a vicious rumor can destroy someone's reputation just as effectively as a physical blow. The word often appears in descriptions of fights, criticism, or competition that goes beyond what feels fair or reasonable, such as a vicious cycle of debt that keeps getting worse. Vicious behavior usually leaves lasting damage, not just a temporary setback.

examples: The dancers moved across the stage in a whirling blur of color and motion.
رقصنده‌ها در صحنه با چرخشی سریع و رنگارنگ حرکت می‌کردند.
A whirling tornado tore through the small town, destroying several houses in minutes.
یک گردباد چرخان شهر کوچک را در عرض چند دقیقه ویران کرد و چند خانه را از بین برد.
She felt dizzy from the whirling carnival ride that spun faster with every second.
او از سوار شدن روی وسیله تفریحی چرخانی که هر لحظه سریع‌تر می‌چرخید، احساس سرگیجه کرد.
miniContext: Something whirling spins or turns rapidly around a central point, often creating a sense of motion or even dizziness. A whirling dancer twirls gracefully across a stage, while a whirling storm like a tornado can cause serious destruction as it spins across the land. People also describe a whirling mind when their thoughts are racing too fast to organize clearly. The image of something whirling almost always suggests speed, energy, and a loss of steady control.

examples: The news reported a violent storm that knocked down power lines across the city.
خبرها از طوفانی خشن خبر دادند که خطوط برق را در سراسر شهر قطع کرد.
Witnesses described the protest as violent after several cars were set on fire.
شاهدان اعتراض را خشونت‌آمیز توصیف کردند، چرا که چند خودرو به آتش کشیده شد.
He has a violent temper and sometimes shouts when he feels frustrated.
او خلق‌وخویی خشن دارد و گاهی وقتی احساس ناکامی می‌کند فریاد می‌زند.
miniContext: Something violent involves physical force intended to hurt, damage, or destroy, whether caused by people, weather, or emotion. A violent crime leaves victims injured or worse, while a violent storm can uproot trees and flood entire neighborhoods. People also describe strong emotions as violent, such as a violent outburst of anger that seems to come out of nowhere. Because the word carries such a strong sense of danger, it is rarely used lightly.
